value.body: A mobile app developer builds and maintains apps for Android and iOS phones. IT services firms, product companies, startups and agencies hire them. A day involves writing app code, fixing bugs, connecting to back-end APIs and testing on devices.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Kotlin, Swift, Flutter or React Native, Git

items.label: Tech industry workforce
items.note: Direct employees across India's IT and tech-services industry at the end of FY 2024-25, with ~1.3 lakh added that year; covers all roles, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join through campus placement, internships or off-campus hiring as junior or trainee developers. Published or open-source apps make a strong portfolio for interviews.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Kotlin/Java for Android or Swift for iOS
Cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter or React Native
Working with REST APIs and local storage
Debugging and testing on real devices
UI layout and basic usability principles

value.title: At a glance
items: Some teams work natively on one platform; others use cross-platform tools.
Common next roles: senior mobile developer, mobile lead, full-stack developer.
App store release and review processes add steps not seen in web work.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
